story_ace/akainu.alt: Sakazuki, A Marine admiral who has read you accurately, and who understands that the fastest way to kill a proud man is to say something about his father

story_ace/cover.alt: Cover art for Ace: You were born already sentenced.

story_ace/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Ace: You were born already sentenced.

story_ace/dadan.alt: Curly Dadan, The mountain bandit a Marine vice-admiral handed two children to, and who has complained about it every single day since without ever once putting either of them down

story_ace/deuce.alt: Masked Deuce, The first person to join you, met on an island neither of you meant to be on, and the only man alive who knew you before there was a legend to know

story_ace/garp.alt: Monkey D. Garp, Marine vice-admiral, Luffy’s grandfather, the man who carried you off Baterilla, and the only living person who knows who your father was

story_ace/jinbe.alt: Jinbe, A fish-man of enormous strength who fought you to a standstill over five days and has considered you a friend ever since

story_ace/luffy.alt: Monkey D. Luffy, Seven years old, has followed you for eleven days, and will not be discouraged by anything you have tried so far

story_ace/marco.alt: Marco, First Division Commander, ship’s doctor, and the brother who has watched the old man adopt disasters for twenty years

story_ace/sabo.alt: Sabo, Your first real friend, born into the clean city on the other side of the wall, and the only person you have met who threw away the name he was given

story_ace/shanks.alt: Red-Haired Shanks, An emperor of the sea who gave your little brother a hat, and who becomes an entirely different person the moment you mention his name

story_ace/stage_alabasta.alt: Alabasta: A desert kingdom in the middle of somebody else’s crisis, where Ace walks into a restaurant and finds his brother sitting in it, years older and exactly the same.

story_ace/stage_asl_treehouse.alt: The Treehouse: Planks, rope and stubbornness, forty feet up, built by two people who were not going to ask for help.

story_ace/stage_banaro.alt: Banaro Island: A town that will not exist by evening.

story_ace/stage_dadan_house.alt: The Dadan Family House: A long timber house that smells of smoke, drying meat and cheap alcohol, with nine adults in it who all complain constantly about the two children they would die for.

story_ace/stage_dawn_shore.alt: Dawn Island Shore: Grey sand, a rickety jetty, and the horizon that the two of you have been describing to each other for two years without either of you having seen anything on it.

story_ace/stage_goa_high_town.alt: High Town, Goa: Clean streets, painted shutters, and residents who have arranged their entire lives around not seeing the thing on the other side of their wall.

story_ace/stage_grand_line_port.alt: Grand Line Port: Any of forty towns that all work the same way: a harbour full of flags nobody asks about, a bounty board, a bar where the wrong three sentences start something, and a Marine office pretending not to keep a list.

story_ace/stage_gray_terminal.alt: Gray Terminal: The city’s rubbish, piled into a country.

story_ace/stage_impel_down.alt: Impel Down — Level Six: The floor nobody is released from, where the prisoners are people the world has decided to stop counting.

story_ace/stage_marineford_battlefield.alt: Marineford: The plaza once it stops being a stage.

story_ace/stage_marineford_platform.alt: The Execution Platform: Raised stone above a plaza built to hold a war, with three admirals, a bay full of warships, and the whole of the world’s press arranged to watch one man be made into an argument.

story_ace/stage_moby_dick_deck.alt: The Moby Dick — Deck: A whale-headed ship the size of a district, with an old man in a chair at the centre of it who is bigger than the chair should allow.

story_ace/stage_moby_dick_mess.alt: The Moby Dick — Mess: Where the Fourth Division feeds four hundred people twice a day and where every relationship on this ship is actually formed.

story_ace/stage_mt_colubo.alt: Mount Colubo: Forest steep enough that the paths are really just the places where fewer things grow.

story_ace/stage_sixis.alt: Sixis: A deserted island at the ragged edge of the East Blue, with fresh water, no people, and one other man who is also pretending he meant to be here.

story_ace/stage_spade_ship.alt: The Spade: A ship bought, stolen or won depending on how it went, crewed by people who chose a captain younger than most of them.

story_ace/stage_whitebeard_medical.alt: The Moby Dick — Medical Bay: Marco’s domain, and the one room on this ship that is quiet.

story_ace/teach.alt: Marshall D. Teach, A Second Division man under your command, patient for decades, and the one person aboard who believes exactly what you believe and drew the opposite conclusion from it

story_ace/thatch.alt: Thatch, Fourth Division Commander, runs the galley, and the reason four hundred people on this ship know each other

story_ace/whitebeard.alt: Edward Newgate, The strongest man in the world, captain of the ship you came to take, and a father to four hundred people who all chose him

story_blackwake/cover.alt: Cover art for Blackwake: A broken ship. Nobody knows your name.

story_blackwake/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Blackwake: A broken ship. Nobody knows your name.

story_blackwake/harrow_bell.alt: Harrow Bell, Broker at the Drift

story_blackwake/mako.alt: Mako Renn, Diver, sixteen, absolutely certain

story_blackwake/nessa.alt: Nessa Vale, Navigator, wanted in three ports

story_blackwake/stage_saltmarket.alt: Saltmarket: Four hundred years of harbour built on top of itself.

story_blackwake/stage_stormlee.alt: Stormlee: An island inside a storm that has not stopped in living memory.

story_blackwake/stage_the_crownless.alt: The Crownless Sea: Nine hundred square miles of water that is on no chart printed in ninety years, and everything in it that is the reason for that.

story_blackwake/stage_the_drift.alt: The Drift: A lawless port built across nine hulks lashed together and grown into each other.

story_blackwake/stage_the_marrow.alt: The Marrow: Forty feet of forty-year-old cutter with a cracked keel, one suit of tired sails, and nobody aboard her but you.

story_blackwake/stage_the_yard.alt: Corrow’s Yard: A slipway, three sheds, and a woman who can tell you what is wrong with your ship from sixty feet away and will, at length.

story_blackwake/tolla.alt: Tolla Corrow, Shipwright, owns the yard

story_blackwake/veyra.alt: Captain Veyra Sol, Ninth Fleet, inshore squadron

story_blank_prophecy/cover.alt: Cover art for The Blank Prophecy: They read your future. It was empty.

story_blank_prophecy/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for The Blank Prophecy: They read your future. It was empty.

story_blank_prophecy/despina.alt: Despina Vlahos, Keeps a guesthouse where the kitchen has never been shut when somebody needed it open, and has kept the oldest rule in the world for thirty years

story_blank_prophecy/eirene.alt: Eirene Sallas, The oracle who read you at Delphi, got nothing, and kept the failed reading against nineteen years of her own procedure

story_blank_prophecy/hecate.alt: Hecate, The one whose whole domain is the place between things, met at a junction on the edge of Athens with a shoebox shrine in a wall

story_blank_prophecy/hermes.alt: Hermes, The one who turns up because he is curious, wants something, and is completely upfront about both

story_blank_prophecy/key.alt: Key art for The Blank Prophecy

story_blank_prophecy/kyros.alt: Kyros Argyros, Twenty-seven, the hero who survived his own prophecy, and the man who has spent four years proving that being told your future is what causes it

story_blank_prophecy/stage_delphi_road.alt: The Road To Delphi: Three hours north-west through mountains, past a service station where the coffee is genuinely excellent, and up into a valley of olive terraces below a cliff with two enormous rocks in it.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_delphi_sanctu.alt: The Sanctuary: Terraces of foundations climbing a mountainside, a theatre, a stadium at the top, and a stone that was once considered the centre of the world by people who were not being metaphorical.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_monastiraki_p.alt: Platform Two: The open-air platform at the interchange with the flea market above it and the ancient road visible through glass at the far end.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_monastiraki_s.alt: The Square And The Lanes: A square with a mosque, a church and a ruin in it, four bars still going, and a warren of lanes behind full of shuttered stalls, cats, and a smell of grilled meat that does not stop until about four.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_piraeus_road.alt: The Port Road: Container cranes, ferry gates, and eleven thousand people a day going to islands.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_plaka_rooftop.alt: The Roofs Under The Rock: Flat concrete roofs with water tanks and washing lines, stepping up the slope towards the floodlit rock, so that a person can cross four streets without touching the ground and be looked down on the whole way by a building that has been there for two and a half thousand years.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_the_council_c.alt: The Chamber In The Rock: Cut into the hill below the temple, older than the temple, and used continuously since.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_the_crossroad.alt: Where Three Ways Meet: A junction on the edge of the city where an old road, a new road and a track that is not on any map come together.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_the_cut_threa.alt: The Warehouse: Forty people who all have a version of the same story, a kitchen, a crèche, and a wall with about nine hundred names on it — every one of them somebody who was told what they were going to do before they had done it.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_the_kerameiko.alt: The Old Burying Ground: Eleven acres of grave markers and foundations below street level, with a stream running through it and tortoises in the grass.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_the_loom.alt: The Loom: Not a machine and not a room.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_the_slope.alt: The Slope: The path round the base of the rock, worn to a shine by three million pairs of feet a year, closed at night and entirely walkable if you know which gate does not lock.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_the_way_down.alt: The Thin Corner: A stair that is not in any plan, going down from a corner of the old burying ground, dry and warm and entirely silent.

story_blank_prophecy/stage_to_xenon.alt: To Xenon: A narrow guesthouse with a kitchen that has never been shut when somebody needed it open.

story_blank_prophecy/thalia.alt: Thalia Kyrkos, Twenty-one, a monster hunter who carries one of Artemis’s Names, and the first person to find out you can see any of this

story_fourth_beast/camille.alt: Camille Laurent, Twenty-one, the other compatible person, and three months into looking for her brother without waiting for anybody to authorise it

story_fourth_beast/cover.alt: Cover art for The Fourth Beast: Three beasts. Two people. You chose first.

story_fourth_beast/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for The Fourth Beast: Three beasts. Two people. You chose first.

story_fourth_beast/key.alt: Key art for The Fourth Beast

story_fourth_beast/lina.alt: Lina Haddad, Journalism student, twenty-three, and the only person in Paris who had the disappearances on one map before anybody official did

story_fourth_beast/lucien.alt: Lucien Marot, Thirty-four, a foundation, a philanthropy budget, a great many people missing, and a creature that chose him rather than the other way round

story_fourth_beast/morel.alt: Étienne Morel, The biologist who grew three animals in a basement because nothing else in the world could touch the man doing this

story_fourth_beast/ravel.alt: Inès Ravel, Commandante, thirty-seven, running six months of linked cases out of a room where the evidence board gets turned around when anybody senior visits

story_fourth_beast/stage_belleville.alt: Belleville: A hill of markets, four cuisines on one street, a park with the whole city laid out below it, and about eleven thousand people who all know each other well enough to notice a stranger and well enough not to mention it to the police.

story_fourth_beast/stage_beraud_lab.alt: The Room Under The Institute: Down two flights from an ordinary research building near the Panthéon: a long low room with grow lights, planted beds and warm air, more greenhouse than laboratory.

story_fourth_beast/stage_canal_saint_mar.alt: Canal Saint-Martin: Iron footbridges, plane trees, locks that take twenty minutes to fill, and people sitting on the quay with a bottle and no intention of moving.

story_fourth_beast/stage_latin_quarter.alt: The Fifth: Bookshops, a cinema that shows the same four films forever, students on the kerb outside a bar at eleven at night, and streets narrow enough that two people cannot pass a delivery scooter without one of them stopping.

story_fourth_beast/stage_lina_flat.alt: The Fourth Floor Walk-Up: One room, a mattress, a desk, and a paper map of Paris on the wall with six months of pins in it.

story_fourth_beast/stage_metro_line.alt: The Métro: Tiled corridors, warm wind ahead of a train, buskers, and the specific silence of a carriage where forty people have all decided not to look at each other.

story_fourth_beast/stage_palais_royal.alt: The Centre: Arcades, gravel gardens, black-and-white columns, a fountain, and the kind of address a foundation with three hundred million euros and a philanthropy budget puts on its letterhead.

story_fourth_beast/stage_police_prefectu.alt: The Prefecture: A great stone building on the island with a courtyard full of parked vehicles and a floor upstairs where nine people have been working six months of linked cases with an evidence board they have started keeping face-down when anybody senior visits.

story_fourth_beast/stage_service_tunnels.alt: The Service Level: Behind the doors that say no entry: cable runs, ventilation plant, disused platforms from lines that were never finished, and a hundred and forty years of the city building underneath itself and forgetting.

story_fourth_beast/stage_the_boundary.alt: Where The Stone Stops: A gallery like every other gallery, except that the far wall is not there and has not been for some time.

story_fourth_beast/stage_the_quarries.alt: The Quarries: A hundred and eighty kilometres of limestone galleries under the south of the city, cut for stone before anybody thought to write down where.

story_fourth_beast/stage_the_roofline.alt: The Roofline: Zinc, chimney stacks, satellite dishes and a two-hundred-year-old drainage arrangement that assumes nobody will ever stand on it.

story_fourth_beast/stage_the_seine.alt: The Riverbank: Stone quays below the traffic, bridges every four hundred metres, and a strip of the city where you can walk for an hour and be visible to almost nobody.

story_fourth_beast/theo.alt: Théo Laurent, Twenty-four, missing since March, and — if anybody gets down there — not dead

story_good_morning_husband/cover.alt: Cover art for Good Morning, Husband: Four years married. You just met her.

story_good_morning_husband/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Good Morning, Husband: Four years married. You just met her.

story_good_morning_husband/emi.alt: Emi Takeda, Hana’s closest friend since art school, and not yours

story_good_morning_husband/hana.alt: Hana Mori, Your wife of four years. Product designer, and the person this whole life is arranged around

story_good_morning_husband/kenji.alt: Kenji Mori, Hana’s older brother. Runs a flooring firm with four vans and eleven opinions

story_good_morning_husband/key.alt: Key art for Good Morning, Husband

story_good_morning_husband/lucia.alt: Lucia Vale, Your best friend in this life, which is a fact you are taking on trust

story_good_morning_husband/nao.alt: Nao Ibarra, Night supervisor at the station, and the only person who will say the platform number out loud

story_good_morning_husband/stage_apartme.alt: Apartment 8B: A living room with a good sofa and a bad rug, eight floors up over a street with a tram on it.

story_good_morning_husband/stage_aster_m.alt: Aster Market Street: Four blocks of greengrocer, hardware shop, a bakery with a queue, and the launderette where the machines are better than the one in the building.

story_good_morning_husband/stage_central.alt: Aster City Central: Ten platforms under a glass roof, a board that flicks, and a night staff of about four.

story_good_morning_husband/stage_hana_st.alt: The Studio: One floor of a converted print works, eleven people, and a wall of models made out of card.

story_good_morning_husband/stage_mori_ho.alt: The Mori House: A narrow house on a hill with too many shoes in the hall and a kitchen that runs at a volume nobody in it considers loud.

story_good_morning_husband/stage_platfor.alt: Platform 11: A platform at the end of the station that the map does not have and the board does not list.

story_good_morning_husband/stage_riversi.alt: Riverside Park: A long green strip beside brown water, a running path, and a bench with a plaque on it that the two of you have a joke about.

story_good_morning_husband/stage_the_bal.alt: The Balcony: Big enough for two chairs if one person turns sideways.

story_good_morning_husband/stage_the_kit.alt: The Kitchen: Four steps from the bed and the brightest room in the flat.

story_good_morning_husband/stage_the_spa.alt: The Spare Room: Eleven square metres containing a drying rack, four boxes nobody has opened since the move, a folded cot still in its packaging, and an exercise bike.

story_good_morning_husband/stage_the_usu.alt: The Usual Place: Nine tables, a specials board nobody has updated since spring, and a couple who run it and have opinions about the two of you.

story_hush_house/ayame.alt: Ayame Kurose, Room 314. Four years into an investigation nobody asked her to run

story_hush_house/cover.alt: Cover art for Hush House: Do not open the door at 2:13 a.m.

story_hush_house/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Hush House: Do not open the door at 2:13 a.m.

story_hush_house/mika.alt: Mika Kurose, Missing four years. Present more often than that should allow

story_hush_house/nia.alt: Nia Bell, Room 405. Art student, and the building’s uninvited documentarian

story_hush_house/stage_bellweather.alt: Bellweather Street: Wet brick, tram wire, two newer buildings crowding Hush House on either side, and a police precinct four hundred metres down where a four-year-old file sits in a drawer.

story_hush_house/stage_floor_zero.alt: Floor 0: The lift opens on a corridor with a window at the end of it.

story_hush_house/stage_hall_third.alt: The Third-Floor Hallway: Six doors, a runner carpet worn down the middle, and a wall light outside 309 that is on a different circuit from all the others.

story_hush_house/stage_konbini.alt: The Konbini: Open all night, lit like an operating theatre, and the only place on this street where nothing has ever happened.

story_hush_house/stage_lobby.alt: The Lobby: Black and white tiles, a lift with a folding brass gate, and Mrs Vale’s desk under the stairs with a lamp on it whatever the hour.

story_hush_house/stage_morrowgate.alt: The Rest of Morrowgate: Everything that is not this street: the ambulance station off Carrow Row where Tomas signs on, the art school Nia is technically enrolled at, the records office where Ayame has a job she will not discuss, and about four hundred thousand people who have never heard of Bellweather Street.

story_hush_house/stage_rooftop.alt: The Roof: Asphalt, a water tank, and a view over the old quarter to the harbour.

story_hush_house/stage_room_206.alt: Room 206: Tomas Reed’s, and the tidiest room in the building because he is almost never in it.

story_hush_house/stage_room_309.alt: Room 309: Empty for four years and still furnished.

story_hush_house/stage_room_312.alt: Room 312: Better than the price suggests: hardwood, a tall bay window over the street, a radiator that comes on by itself at ten.

story_hush_house/stage_room_405.alt: Room 405: Nia Bell’s, and the exact opposite: two monitors on a door laid across trestles, cables taped down the skirting, and a corkboard of stills printed at the library with times written under them in marker.

story_hush_house/stage_shared_kitchen.alt: The Shared Kitchen: Half a floor of the third storey, from when this was a boarding house properly.

story_hush_house/stage_stairwell.alt: The Stairwell: Stone treads, an iron rail, and a landing cupboard between every floor.

story_hush_house/stage_sub_basement.alt: The Sub-Basement: Below the legal basement, behind a bricked arch, the floor stops being concrete and becomes dressed stone.

story_hush_house/vale.alt: Mrs Elara Vale, Landlady, fourth of her family to hold the agreement

story_itachi/cover.alt: Cover art for Itachi: Both sides already think you are theirs.

story_itachi/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Itachi: Both sides already think you are theirs.

story_itachi/danzo.alt: Danzo Shimura, The man who runs the part of the village that does not appear on the chart, and who has been extremely polite to you for two years

story_itachi/fugaku.alt: Fugaku Uchiha, Your father, head of the clan, chief of the police the village will not let police anything, and the man organising the coup

story_itachi/hiruzen.alt: Hiruzen Sarutobi, The Third Hokage, who wants a settlement, has wanted one for ten years, and has been outmanoeuvred every year by a man he refuses to remove

story_itachi/izumi.alt: Izumi Uchiha, A clan girl your own age who has decided, on no encouragement whatsoever, that the two of you are friends

story_itachi/kakashi.alt: Kakashi Hatake, Another prodigy who was handed a war at eleven, four years ahead of you on the same road, and the only person in the ready room who has never asked you anything

story_itachi/mikoto.alt: Mikoto Uchiha, Your mother, a retired shinobi nobody in this house treats as one, and the person best placed to mediate if anyone thinks to ask her

story_itachi/sasuke.alt: Sasuke Uchiha, Your brother, seven years old, and the only person in this village who wants nothing from you except your time

story_itachi/shisui.alt: Shisui Uchiha, Your closest friend, four years older, and the only person alive who talks to you as though you are a person rather than an instrument

story_itachi/stage_anbu_ready_room.alt: The Ready Room: Underneath the tower: benches, a rack of masks, a board of assignments written in a hand that changes every three weeks, and a rule that nobody uses a name in here.

story_itachi/stage_hokage_office.alt: The Tower Office: A round room at the top of the tower with too much paper in it and a window that looks at the whole village at once, which is either the point of the job or the trap in it.

story_itachi/stage_izumi_home.alt: The House On The Fourth Street: Two rooms and a yard the width of a door, kept by a woman who has been on her own in it for nine years and a daughter who has started coming home the long way round.

story_itachi/stage_naka_shrine.alt: The Shrine By The River: A small unstaffed shrine with seven tatami mats in its back room.

story_itachi/stage_nakano_cliff.alt: The Cliff Over The River: Where the river turns and the rock stands out over it.

story_itachi/stage_police_headquarters.alt: The Police Building: Three floors, a duty desk, and an entire institution staffed almost exclusively by one family, which is either an honour or a containment depending on which of them you ask.

story_itachi/stage_root_chamber.alt: The Room Under The Village: Stone, dry air, and a table with one chair on the far side of it.

story_itachi/stage_susuki_teahouse.alt: The Tea Place: Six seats and a counter, run by an old woman who has fed three generations of this clan and has opinions about all of them.

story_itachi/stage_the_academy.alt: The School: A low building with a yard, a swing, and a wall of graduation photographs going back forty years.

story_itachi/stage_the_rooftops.alt: The Roofs: The fastest way across this village and the only part of it where nobody is on a schedule.

story_itachi/stage_training_ground.alt: The Posts: Three wooden posts in a clearing with a river behind them, scarred to the height a child can reach and again at the height an adult can.

story_itachi/stage_uchiha_house.alt: The House On The Corner: Four rooms, a stove that needs coaxing, and a step at the front that gets the last of the sun.

story_itachi/stage_uchiha_street.alt: The District: Nine streets of clan houses behind a wall that was built to keep something out and now mostly keeps this lot in.

story_itachi/stage_village_gate.alt: The South Gate: Two enormous wooden doors, a booth with two chunin in it who are bored and thorough in that order, and the road out.

story_last_five/rei.alt: Rei Amagi, Seiran Academy · scoring guard

story_last_five/stage_away_hakuba.alt: Hakuba West: A public school gym with a leaking roof and the best point guard in the prefecture.

story_last_five/stage_away_onda.alt: Onda Commercial: Loudest gym in the prefecture, and most of it is one person talking.

story_last_five/stage_away_seiran.alt: Seiran Academy: A gym with seating for two thousand and a scoreboard that works.

story_last_five/stage_away_tessen.alt: Tessen Industrial: A converted factory floor with a court in it.

story_last_five/stage_film_room.alt: The Film Room: A storage cupboard with a projector in it.

story_last_five/stage_kosei_gym.alt: The Kosei Gym: Two courts, one of them with a dead spot near the left elbow that everybody knows about.

story_last_five/stage_kosei_school.alt: Kosei High: Corridors, a vending machine that only takes exact change, and the staff office where the board’s letter came from.

story_last_five/stage_locker_room.alt: The Locker Room: Eleven lockers, six of them in use.

story_last_five/stage_nationals.alt: The National Championship: Nine thousand seats, a floor laid this morning, and a programme with Kosei printed in it.

story_last_five/tsubame.alt: Tsubame Kirisawa, Hakuba West · point guard

story_last_service/cover.alt: Cover art for Last Service: Thirty seats. Thirty days. One kitchen.

story_last_service/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Last Service: Thirty seats. Thirty days. One kitchen.

story_last_service/daichi.alt: Daichi Ren, Twenty-two, on the Akari line for four years, and reliable in a way nobody has ever thanked him for

story_last_service/emi.alt: Emi Nakahara, Twenty-one, the entire front of house, and the reason this kitchen gets away with anything

story_last_service/haruto.alt: Haruto Gin, Forty-eight, executive chef at VANTA, and the most formidable person in this story because he is not trying to be

story_last_service/keiko.alt: Keiko, Forty-six, your aunt, and the person who has kept this restaurant open for nineteen years

story_last_service/mina.alt: Mina Saegusa, Twenty-four, sous-chef at the best restaurant in the city, and the one they call the knife that never hesitates

story_last_service/reina.alt: Reina Kado, Thirty-five, food critic, and the person in this city whose four hundred words can fill a thirty-seat room for a year

story_last_service/stage_akari_dining.alt: The Akari Dining Room: Thirty seats: eleven at the counter, five tables of two, three of four.

story_last_service/stage_akari_kitchen.alt: The Akari Kitchen: Six metres by three.

story_last_service/stage_akari_office.alt: The Office: A cupboard with a desk in it, a chair that came from the dining room in 2011, a filing box, a wall calendar with a date circled in it, and one page from a ventilation firm that has been sitting on the desk for five weeks.

story_last_service/stage_city_table_hall.alt: The Circuit Hall: A converted market building the city uses for eleven Services over four weeks: benches, gas rings, a scoring table for the ones that have scoring, and about two hundred people standing round the edges eating things off paper.

story_last_service/stage_culinary_school.alt: The Culinary School: Four teaching kitchens, a demonstration theatre and a hundred and forty students who mostly will not still be cooking in six years.

story_last_service/stage_fish_market.alt: The Fish Market: Five in the morning, wet concrete, forty stalls and an auction floor.

story_last_service/stage_keiko_flat.alt: Keiko’s Flat: Two rooms above a laundry six minutes from the restaurant, chosen nineteen years ago because it was six minutes from the restaurant.

story_last_service/stage_night_market.alt: The Night Market: Forty stalls, one street, and a queue outside one of them that has not been under twenty people since March.

story_last_service/stage_reina_office.alt: The Paper: A food desk of three people on the fourth floor of a building with two hundred in it.

story_last_service/stage_supplier_yard.alt: The Supplier’s Yard: A loading bay, a cold store and a small office with a man in it who has known this family for eleven years, likes them, and has an accounts department that does not care about that at all.

story_last_service/stage_the_arcade_stre.alt: The Street: A tram line, a covered arcade, a laundry, a bar with eleven seats and three other places that serve food.

story_last_service/stage_the_back_alley.alt: The Back Alley: Two metres of wet concrete between the back door and the bins, with a crate everybody sits on, an extractor outlet above it and a view of exactly one strip of sky.

story_last_service/stage_the_hotel.alt: The Hotel Kitchen: A banquet operation doing four hundred covers of one menu, with a brigade of twenty and a system that works whether or not anybody in it is inspired.

story_last_service/stage_vanta.alt: VANTA: Eighteen covers a sitting, two sittings, a kitchen with eleven people in it and a pass that never raises its voice.

story_last_service/takumi.alt: Takumi Arashi, Twenty-three, one burner and a griddle at the night market, four hundred covers a night, and a queue that has not been under twenty since March

story_light/aizawa.alt: Shuichi Aizawa, A detective with a mortgage and two children, who will distrust you by a route that has nothing to do with L’s reasoning

story_light/cover.alt: Cover art for Light: Everyone thinks they could beat L.

story_light/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Light: Everyone thinks they could beat L.

story_light/kaito.alt: Kaito Serizawa, The boy behind you, who will ask for your notes on the way out and has been asking for two years

story_light/l.alt: L, The best detective alive, who is childish about losing, who is not psychic, and who will know exactly as much as your actions have made knowable

story_light/matsuda.alt: Touta Matsuda, The youngest man on the task force, underestimated by everybody including himself, and the only one who talks to you like a person

story_light/mello.alt: Mello, The other one, who would rather take a risk that kills him than come second, and who breaks plans by refusing to behave like an investigator

story_light/mikami.alt: Teru Mikami, A prosecutor who worships Kira absolutely, who is disciplined to the point of rigidity, and who will do exactly what he is explicitly told

story_light/misa.alt: Misa Amane, A famous model with a second notebook, who worships Kira for killing the man who murdered her parents, and who is not remotely stupid

story_light/naomi.alt: Naomi Misora, A former FBI agent who is better at this than the man she was going to marry, and who will only ever become your problem if you make her one

story_light/near.alt: Near, One of two children raised to replace L, who inherits the evidence and reasons independently from it, and who is not a white-haired copy of him

story_light/raye.alt: Raye Penber, An FBI agent assigned to watch twelve people connected to the investigation, one of whom is you, and who is about four days from clearing you

story_light/rem.alt: Rem, Misa’s Shinigami, who is attached to her in a way Ryuk is attached to nobody, and who does not trust you at all

story_light/ryuk.alt: Ryuk, The Shinigami who dropped the notebook, who is here because he was bored, and who does not care whether you win

story_light/sachiko.alt: Sachiko Yagami, Your mother, who is proud of you out loud and worried about your father in silence, and who cleans your room every week

story_light/sayu.alt: Sayu Yagami, Your sister, fourteen, who admires you completely and wants help with her maths homework

story_light/soichiro.alt: Soichiro Yagami, Your father, superintendent of the NPA, a man of extraordinary integrity, and the reason the most valuable intelligence in the country is in your hallway

story_light/stage_confinement.alt: Confinement: A bare room, a camera, a blindfold, and fifty days.

story_light/stage_daikoku_classroom.alt: Daikoku Private Academy: Third floor, window side, last period.

story_light/stage_gamou_prep.alt: Gamou Prep School: A crowded room of people working extremely hard at something he finds effortless, which is where he goes when the house is too warm to think in.

story_light/stage_hotel_taskforce.alt: The Task Force Hotel: A suite with the beds taken out and monitors put in, six exhausted policemen, a great deal of cake, and a man sitting on a chair in a way chairs are not for.

story_light/stage_interpol.alt: The ICPO Conference: A room of senior police from every country, addressed by a laptop.

story_light/stage_kanto_street.alt: Kanto: Trains, crossings, station concourses, convenience stores and the particular anonymity of a city where nobody looks at anybody.

story_light/stage_light_bedroom.alt: Light’s Bedroom: A desk under the window, textbooks in order of use, and a drawer with a false bottom in it.

story_light/stage_mello_mafia.alt: The Mafia Base: A converted industrial building in Los Angeles run by somebody who would rather take a risk that kills him than come second to the boy on the carpet.

story_light/stage_misa_apartment.alt: Misa’s Apartment: Expensive, cluttered, lit like a magazine shoot, with clothes on every surface and a diary on the table that should not exist.

story_light/stage_nhn_studio.alt: The NHN Studio: A broadcast set from which one woman reads Kira’s position to the country every evening, in a voice designed to make it sound like the weather.

story_light/stage_spk_hq.alt: SPK Headquarters: A New York office with a boy sitting on the floor in the middle of it, building something out of dice, surrounded by people who have decided to take him seriously.

story_light/stage_taskforce_hq.alt: Task Force Headquarters: Eight floors of building put up for this one case, with a lift that needs a code and a basement nobody discusses.

story_light/stage_tooh_university.alt: To-Oh University: Where two people who came joint first in the entrance examination give the freshman address together, and then play tennis in front of everybody, and both of them know exactly what the tennis is.

story_light/stage_yagami_home.alt: The Yagami House: A warm middle-class house in which somebody is always cooking and somebody is always late.

story_light/stage_yellow_box.alt: The Yellow Box Warehouse: An abandoned building with catwalks, stacked crates, holes in the roof and rain coming through them, chosen by somebody who wanted the last conversation of his life to happen somewhere he had picked.

story_light/stage_yotsuba_boardroom.alt: The Yotsuba Boardroom: Eight executives around a table deciding which people in the world are inconvenient to their quarterly figures, in the tone of men discussing a logistics contract.

story_nine_weeks/stage_kitchen.alt: The Kitchen: Hot, loud, and the actual centre of this building.

story_nine_weeks/stage_longhouse_bar.alt: The Longhouse Bar: A long room with the lake down one whole side and a small stage at the end that gets used more nights than not.

story_nine_weeks/stage_staff_cabins.alt: The Staff Cabins: Six timber cabins behind the car park, four bunks each, a shared bathroom with one good shower.

story_nine_weeks/stage_the_dock.alt: The Dock: Boards out over the water, four boats tied up, and the only place on the property where you can be seen by everyone and overheard by nobody.

story_nine_weeks/stage_the_point.alt: The Point: A shingle spit on the far shore with one dead tree on it, twenty minutes across the water and out of sight of the whole property.

story_nine_weeks/stage_town_road.alt: The Road Into Town: Twenty minutes of tarmac with no lights on it, walked at two in the morning by people who wanted twenty minutes of not being at work.

story_ninth_archive/stage_archive_floor.alt: Archive Reading Floor: Eight doors, eight brass numerals, and a reading floor between them where the lamps are kept deliberately low.

story_ninth_archive/stage_archive_stacks.alt: The Stacks: Rolling shelves on iron rails, packed close enough that you have to crank a gap to walk.

story_ninth_archive/stage_commons.alt: The Commons: A long hall of scarred oak tables where the Academy pretends to be a school.

story_ninth_archive/stage_dorm.alt: Your Room: A bed, a desk, a window that does not quite close, and a door the Academy has a key to.

story_ninth_archive/stage_gate_arch.alt: The Gate Arch: Verath’s outer arch, wide enough for four abreast and warded to read every one of them.

story_ninth_archive/stage_lecture_hall.alt: Arcane Lecture Hall: Steep banked benches around a demonstration well.

story_ninth_archive/stage_rooftop.alt: The Leads: Flat lead sheeting between two gables, out of the wind and out of the wards.

story_ninth_archive/stage_warden_office.alt: The Warden's Office: Warm, tidy, and hung with student portraits going back sixty years.

story_ninth_archive/ysolde.alt: Warden Ysolde Farrow, Warden of Records

story_pink_tide/adrian.alt: Adrian Vale, Thirty-four, documentary producer, missing since Tuesday night, and alive on a ledge under the east cliffs

story_pink_tide/celeste.alt: Celeste Ward, Twenty-seven, fashion influencer on a sponsored stay, and the accidental owner of the only photographs that matter

story_pink_tide/cover.alt: Cover art for Pink Tide: Paradise. One week. One missing man.

story_pink_tide/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Pink Tide: Paradise. One week. One missing man.

story_pink_tide/eli.alt: Eli Mercer, Thirty-one, assistant manager, nine years from the front desk to the fourth floor, and awake since Tuesday

story_pink_tide/june.alt: June Kato, Twenty-six, night bartender on the roof, and the best-informed person on this island

story_pink_tide/luka.alt: Luka Reyes, Twenty-five, dive instructor, and the person who understands the water round this island better than anybody who has ever managed it

story_pink_tide/marcus.alt: Marcus Vane, Thirty-nine, regional development executive, in villa nine for the expansion meetings

story_pink_tide/nami.alt: Nami Kuroda, Twenty-nine, marine biologist contracted to the expansion assessment, and the person who started all of this with one anonymous email

story_pink_tide/reika.alt: Reika Mori, Forty-six, general manager of Aster Cove, and the only person on this island who can halt anything

story_pink_tide/sora.alt: Sora Amemiya, Twenty-three, third summer as a guest-experience host, and the reason most people remember this island

story_pink_tide/stage_adrian_room.alt: Ocean Tower 808: Cleaned to a standard the rest of the hotel does not quite reach.

story_pink_tide/stage_beach_club.alt: The Beach Club: White sand, sixty loungers, a volleyball net that gets serious after five, paddleboards stacked by colour, and a kitchen doing plates of grilled fish and cold beer until sunset.

story_pink_tide/stage_dive_centre.alt: The Dive Centre: Tanks in racks, a compressor that runs at seven, a whiteboard with tide times and today’s sites, and a laminated map of the coast with one area politely crossed out.

story_pink_tide/stage_east_cove.alt: East Cove: Closed for marina-expansion surveys, which is partly true.

story_pink_tide/stage_ferry_dock.alt: The Ferry Dock: A covered berth, a bench, a luggage trolley and a board with four crossings a day on it.

story_pink_tide/stage_infinity_pool.alt: The Infinity Pool: Forty metres of turquoise with no visible far edge, so the water appears to run straight into the ocean.

story_pink_tide/stage_lighthouse.alt: The Old Lighthouse: Decommissioned eleven years ago and left standing because it is beautiful.

story_pink_tide/stage_pink_tide_shore.alt: The Pink Tide Shore: Ten minutes along the sand from the beach club, away from every light the resort owns.

story_pink_tide/stage_rooftop_bar.alt: The Rooftop Bar: Eleven floors up, open to the sky, a pool you are not supposed to swim in and a view of the whole island — the pool, the beach, the marina lights, and the dark unlit stretch of coast to the east that nobody has explained to you.

story_pink_tide/stage_sea_cave.alt: The Sea Cave: A tidal mouth under the east cliffs that is open around low water and closed the rest of the time.

story_pink_tide/stage_service_corridors.alt: The Service Corridors: Bare concrete and strip light behind all that marble.

story_pink_tide/stage_staff_backstep.alt: The Staff Backstep: Three concrete steps, a bin, an ashtray and a view of the generator.

story_pink_tide/stage_the_lobby.alt: The Lobby: Cool marble after the heat, a wall of glass onto the water, orchids that are replaced every second day, and a front desk with three people behind it who have never once said no to anybody.

story_pink_tide/stage_the_marina.alt: The Marina: Forty berths, a fuel dock, two resort launches and a row of private boats belonging to people who did not come here on the ferry.

story_pink_tide/stage_the_villas.alt: The Private Villas: Forty of them along the headland, each with a plunge pool, a golf buggy and a gate.

story_pink_tide/stage_watersports_shed.alt: The Watersports Shed: Timber, salt-bleached, padlocked at night.

story_pink_tide/stage_your_room.alt: Your Room: Better than you expected.

story_primal_crown/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Primal Crown: The herds moved early. Somebody loses.

story_primal_crown/ilya.alt: Ilya Crest, Skyfire scout and information broker, who has already sold what he knows about the north to two different peoples and is open to a third

story_primal_crown/kaia.alt: Kaia Thorn, Emberclaw raptor rider, the fastest at this crossing, and the one who will still be arguing about the corridor when everybody else has gone to bed

story_primal_crown/mako.alt: Mako Reed, Mireborn healer and river guide, who will treat your animal for nothing and then tell you exactly what you did to it

story_primal_crown/stage_ashen_camp.alt: The Broken Ground: Four hide shelters in a fold of rock below the ridge, three cages, and a great deal of fired clay.

story_primal_crown/stage_blackglass_ridg.alt: Blackglass Ridge: A spine of volcanic rock that has been warm underfoot since spring, with new cracks in it and a smell of eggs on the wind.

story_primal_crown/stage_emberclaw_groun.alt: The Emberclaw Ground: Not a camp so much as a wide flat area with tents around the edge and a great deal of racing in the middle.

story_primal_crown/stage_frostfang_fires.alt: The Frostfang Fires: Nine fires in a wide ring with sleeping platforms between them, and a quiet you can hear from three hundred feet away.

story_primal_crown/stage_market_lanes.alt: The Market Lanes: Six hundred stalls in four crooked rows, roofed with hide against a sun that has not properly arrived yet.

story_primal_crown/stage_mireborn_landin.alt: The Landing: Floating walkways, reed matting and a dozen flat boats poled up from the delta, with hadrosaurs standing chest-deep alongside them chewing.

story_primal_crown/stage_skyfire_perch.alt: The Perch: A finger of rock two hundred feet above the crossing with a rope stair up the back of it and no railing anywhere.

story_primal_crown/stage_southern_grass.alt: The Southern Grass: What all of this is about.

story_primal_crown/stage_stoneback_wharf.alt: The Stoneback Wharf: Timber, rope, cranes worked by animals the size of houses, and more written record than the rest of this crossing put together.

story_primal_crown/stage_the_bone_caves.alt: The Bone Caves: Three chambers in a limestone bluff, floored with the bones of animals nobody at this crossing has a name for.

story_primal_crown/stage_the_north_road.alt: The North Road: Not a road.

story_primal_crown/stage_the_picket_line.alt: The Picket Lines: Half a mile of staked ground where four thousand animals are tethered by people who do not entirely trust each other’s animals.

story_primal_crown/stage_the_stone_circl.alt: The Circle: A flat hide the size of a room, pegged into the ground, with five carved river stones laid on it in a pattern forty years old.

story_primal_crown/suri.alt: Suri Snow, Frostfang sabertooth rider, here to secure the northern herd routes, and the person at this crossing who talks least and notices most

story_primal_crown/torren.alt: Torren Vale, Stoneback heir and negotiator, whose family holds the corridor survey everybody is arguing from, and who is a great deal sharper than his manners suggest

story_primal_crown/vesh.alt: Vesh Ardan, A beast-breaker with no colours who sells difficult animals at the pickets and is extremely good at it

story_red_floor/aya.alt: Aya Kisaragi, Twenty-three, nationally ranked, a pressure fighter who teaches people to be frightened of standing still

story_red_floor/cover.alt: Cover art for The Red Floor: No cameras. No records. Step on or do not.

story_red_floor/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for The Red Floor: No cameras. No records. Step on or do not.

story_red_floor/daigo.alt: Daigo Kurosaki, World champion, thirty-one, trains in a warehouse an hour out of the city with eleven people and no press

story_red_floor/junpei.alt: Junpei Arata, Thirty-four, former national champion, stopped twice in his last five, and frightened of Mondays

story_red_floor/key.alt: Key art for The Red Floor

story_red_floor/koji.alt: Koji Namba, Twenty-eight, journeyman, works in his uncle’s print shop, has lost a great deal and loves this anyway

story_red_floor/maki.alt: Tetsuo Maki, Fifty-eight, owns Mikado, keeps the floor, and once asked a boxer for one more round and got it

story_red_floor/mei.alt: Mei Hoshino, Thirty-two, sports physician, former high-level judoka, and the only person in this story whose no actually means no

story_red_floor/riku.alt: Riku Seno, Twenty-two, a professional boxer with a proper gym and a proper team, who comes down to a basement on Sundays anyway

story_red_floor/stage_daigo_camp.alt: The Camp: A converted warehouse an hour out of the city where a world champion trains with eleven people and no press.

story_red_floor/stage_junpei_flat.alt: The Eleventh Floor: One room and a kitchen in a residential tower, with a bed, a table, a television that is never on and almost nothing else.

story_red_floor/stage_koji_print_shop.alt: Namba Printing: A two-man print and packaging business in a side street, run by a man and his nephew, with a guillotine, three machines of different ages and a radio that has been on the same station since 2009.

story_red_floor/stage_mei_clinic.alt: The Clinic: Sports medicine and rehab on the first floor of a modern building, with a gym at the back that is better equipped than Mikado and a waiting room containing four people who all know each other.

story_red_floor/stage_mikado_gym.alt: Mikado Gym: Second floor of an old mixed-use building above a restaurant, up a staircase with a bend in it.

story_red_floor/stage_seno_gym.alt: Seno Boxing: A proper professional operation eleven minutes from Mikado: two rings, air conditioning, a sponsor board, a physio on site and a wall of photographs of people who have gone somewhere.

story_red_floor/stage_the_arcade.alt: The Shopping Arcade: Four hundred metres of roofed arcade with three shutters permanently down, a fishmonger, a stationers, a bar with eleven seats and a convenience store at the far end that is the only thing open at four in the morning.

story_red_floor/stage_the_arena.alt: Kurohama Arena: Four thousand seats, a proper canvas, commission officials, a doctor at ringside and a broadcast truck outside.

story_red_floor/stage_the_hill.alt: The Hill: Nine hundred metres at about eleven per cent, at the end of the seawall, with a vending machine at the top that has been broken since spring.

story_red_floor/stage_the_office.alt: The Office: Two metres by three, a desk, a kettle, a filing cabinet with a drawer that does not open, and a wall with eleven picture hooks in it and one photograph hanging on the second hook from the left.

story_red_floor/stage_the_red_floor.alt: The Red Floor: The old storage level, low-ceilinged, with faded dark red mats laid across the whole of it.

story_red_floor/stage_the_waterfront.alt: The Waterfront: A container terminal, a fish market that starts at four, and about two kilometres of seawall with a hill at the end of it that everybody in this sport in this city has run up at five in the morning and hated.

story_red_floor/stage_the_weigh_in.alt: The Function Room: A hotel function room with a scale on a low stage, a backdrop with eleven logos on it, and about forty people who all want something specific from the next ninety seconds.

story_red_moon/ren.alt: Ren Calder, The other recruit who was going to be first

story_red_moon/serah.alt: Commander Serah Vale, The Brigade’s commander

story_red_moon/stage_ash_flats.alt: The Ash Flats: Twelve miles of pale grit where a forest used to be.

story_red_moon/stage_fort_ember.alt: Fort Ember: Barracks, armoury, muster yard and mess, all built into the inside face of the city wall.

story_red_moon/stage_infirmary.alt: The Infirmary: Thirty beds, eleven occupied, and a smell of iodine that gets into your coat.

story_red_moon/stage_outer_gate.alt: The Outer Gate: Two doors of banded iron, forty feet high, and a killing yard behind them.

story_red_moon/stage_sunken_town.alt: Kelder’s Reach: A town a Behemoth walked through eleven years ago.

story_red_moon/stage_the_ramparts.alt: The Ramparts: Forty feet up, wide enough for four abreast, and open to whatever the wind is carrying.

story_red_moon/stage_the_undercroft.alt: The Undercroft: Below the specimen hall, behind a door with a sixty-year-old lock.

story_red_moon/stage_vale_office.alt: Commander Vale’s Office: One desk, one map, one chair for visitors, and sixty years of the Brigade in the things on the walls.

story_red_moon/stage_voss_lab.alt: The Specimen Hall: Two floors underground, and colder than the rest of the fort by design.

story_red_moon/wick.alt: Wick, Someone else the Behemoths did not finish

story_salt_road/stage_first_well.alt: The First Well: A stone ring and a windlass that works.

story_salt_road/stage_ossun_gate.alt: Ossun Gate: The last wall before the flats.

story_salt_road/stage_second_well.alt: The Second Well: Sound, deep, and crowded.

story_salt_road/stage_the_wrecks.alt: The Wrecks: Four wagons in a rough line, upright, still loaded.

story_salt_road/stage_third_well.alt: The Third Well: Marked with a question mark on every map worth having.

story_second_skin/edran.alt: Edran Sol, Fifty-six, High Keeper of the Concord, and the most persuasive person in this story

story_second_skin/ilyra.alt: Ilyra Morn, Thirty-four, Captain of the Crown Wardens in Larkspire, and the officer whose lawful duty is bringing Kaia Voss in

story_second_skin/kaia.alt: Kaia Voss, Twenty-two, former Roadwarden, wanted, and the only person you have ever seen with two shapes

story_second_skin/lio.alt: Lio Voss, Eighteen, officially dead for fourteen months, and living in a clean warm room under the capital

story_second_skin/ren.alt: Maren Tovi, Sixteen, chose Wolf in front of four generations of Wolf Wardens, and wanted Hawk

story_second_skin/sai.alt: Sai Velo, Twenty-nine, Concord physician, and the author of a protocol his own institution has declined to publish

story_second_skin/stage_aurelion_gate.alt: The Capital Gate: Eleven days south: white walls, a river, a Concord seat with a dome on it, and somewhere under all of that a ward with a number rather than a name.

story_second_skin/stage_concord_house.alt: The Concord House: Green and cream, a waiting hall with forty people in it on any given morning, free draughts for anybody in their first year, and a records floor above that is the only part of the building with a lock on the door.

story_second_skin/stage_heartstone_hall.alt: The Heartstone Hall: Pale stone, four hundred people and a gallery running round three sides at the height a Hawk would use.

story_second_skin/stage_larkspire_market.alt: The Market Streets: Pale stone and red tile, canals, hanging gardens and a crowd built out of about forty different body plans.

story_second_skin/stage_player_home.alt: Home: Three rooms up a stair with a bend in it, chairs in two different back designs, a doorway that somebody widened eleven years ago for a relative, and a cord in your family’s colours that took eleven days to braid.

story_second_skin/stage_sai_infirmary.alt: The Infirmary On The Water: Two rooms over a boat-builder, run by a Concord physician who is officially doing outreach and unofficially doing something else.

story_second_skin/stage_the_canal_quarte.alt: The Canal Quarter: Where the water and the trade meet: barges, warm rooms let by the week to Serpents and anybody else who wants one, an eel market, and about eleven inns whose keepers have all agreed not to ask anybody anything.

story_second_skin/stage_the_far_road.alt: The Far Road: North out of the city gate and up: eleven days of trade road with messenger towers on the high points, inns with warm rooms, and Roadwardens who will walk with you for a stretch if the weather turns.

story_second_skin/stage_the_rails.alt: The Rails: The upper city: landing rails on every third roof, rope walks, gutters wide enough to run, and an entire second set of streets that about a third of the population uses daily and the rest have never been on.

story_second_skin/stage_the_undercroft.alt: The Undercroft: Under the hall, around the top of the thing itself, which is warm and enormous and moves about eleven times an hour.

story_second_skin/stage_veyr_pass.alt: Veyr Pass: A high northern town on a shelf of rock with a Roadwarden station, four hundred people and a great deal of snow.

story_second_skin/stage_ward_seven.alt: Secondary Echo Ward Seven: Clean, warm, well-lit and underground.

story_second_skin/stage_warden_post.alt: The Warden Post: Navy and gold, a duty desk, a board of notices and eleven people whose actual job is stopping civilians being hurt and who are extremely good at it.

story_second_skin/tessa.alt: Tessa Vale, Sixteen, chose Hawk, and has wanted the far-road courier network since she was nine

story_seven_days/mina.alt: Mina Arclight, The first person you meet, every Monday

story_seven_days/stage_boarding_house.alt: The Boarding House: Four rooms, a landlady who does not ask questions, and a kitchen you are allowed to use until nine.

story_seven_days/stage_council_hall.alt: The Council Hall: Municipal, 1890s, and much too big for a town this size.

story_seven_days/stage_the_clock_tower.alt: The Clock Tower: Top of the hill, ninety feet, and stopped at 11:59 since before anybody alive was born.

story_seven_days/stage_the_esplanade.alt: The Esplanade: A curve of shopfronts facing the water.

story_seven_days/stage_the_library.alt: The Public Library: One room upstairs above the old assembly hall.

story_seven_days/stage_the_marina.alt: The Marina: Eighty berths, maybe thirty of them used.

story_seven_days/stage_the_old_town.alt: The Old Town: Six streets of stone cottages above the front, most of them holiday lets.

story_seven_days/stage_the_platform.alt: Halcyon Bay Station: One platform, a canopy with a hole in it, and a view straight down the hill to the water.

story_seven_days/stage_the_point.alt: The Point: The headland past the marina.

story_seven_days/theo.alt: Theo Marr, The boy at the middle table

story_seven_days/wynn.alt: Detective Sera Wynn, Investigating something that has not happened yet

story_seven_names/anais.alt: Anaïs Bellier, Thirty-nine, physician, and the woman whose signature made the prosecution’s timeline possible

story_seven_names/celeste.alt: Céleste Varenne, Twenty-four, a financier’s daughter, and — three nights a week under another name — the best burglar in Paris

story_seven_names/cover.alt: Cover art for Seven Names: You hang at dawn. Unless you go now.

story_seven_names/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Seven Names: You hang at dawn. Unless you go now.

story_seven_names/marcel.alt: Marcel Bellac, Sixty-three, prisoner forty-seven, a forger by trade, and six years into a tunnel he started before he knew what he would do with it

story_seven_names/renaud.alt: Gabriel Renaud, Inspector, thirty-two, junior on the Valère case, and the only man in France who has never signed off on your drowning

story_seven_names/solene.alt: Solène Artois, Forty-four, owner of six newspapers, and the person who turned you from a suspect into a national monster in nine days

story_seven_names/stage_bellier_surgery.alt: The Surgery: Two rooms over a pharmacy south of the river, a waiting bench, and a doctor who takes patients who cannot pay on Tuesdays.

story_seven_names/stage_le_matin_offices.alt: Le Matin Français: Six floors of a building that decides what four hundred thousand people think before breakfast.

story_seven_names/stage_marseille_docks.alt: The Marseille Docks: Forty berths of coal, wine, soap and people, a customs house that operates on the honour system and a great deal of money, and eleven languages being shouted before six in the morning.

story_seven_names/stage_marseille_room.alt: The Room Over The Laundry: One franc fifty a night, no register, a window onto a courtyard with four exits from it, and steam coming up through the floor at all hours from the laundry below.

story_seven_names/stage_paris_hotel.alt: The Hôtel Beaumont: Where it happened.

story_seven_names/stage_prefecture.alt: The Prefecture: The whole apparatus in one building: records, magistrates, the archive of the Valère case in eleven boxes, and an inspector on the third floor who has never signed off on a drowning he does not believe in.

story_seven_names/stage_saint_charles.alt: Saint-Charles Station: A great glass shed at the top of a flight of stairs, with the Paris express standing at platform three for eleven hours a day and two men in plain coats at the barrier who are not railway employees and are not hiding it.

story_seven_names/stage_serein_cell.alt: The Cell: Four paces by three, a bed, a bucket, and a window too narrow to put a shoulder through.

story_seven_names/stage_serein_tunnel.alt: The Tunnel: Six years of work: a crawl through fill and rubble, shored with bed slats, running under two corridors and out through the old cistern to the seaward wall.

story_seven_names/stage_service_passage.alt: The Service Passage: Eleven metres of unlit corridor between the kitchens and the cloakrooms, with a door at each end and a bend in the middle.

story_seven_names/stage_the_boulevards.alt: The Boulevards: Cafés, kiosks, a tram, six evening papers on sale by four in the afternoon and a great many people who read all of them.

story_seven_names/stage_the_express.alt: The Paris Express: Fourteen hours, three classes, a dining car and a corridor that everybody on this train will walk down at least twice.

story_seven_names/stage_the_opera.alt: The Opera: Where everybody who matters is visible for three hours on the same evening, in boxes, at known heights, in a building with more corridors behind the boxes than in front of them.

story_seven_names/stage_the_seaward_wall.alt: The Seaward Wall: The bottom of the fortress where the rock meets black water, a gate that has not been opened since the eighties, and eleven kilometres of Mediterranean between here and a coast with lights on it.

story_seven_names/stage_the_vault.alt: The Vault: Not a vault and not one place: three rooms in three buildings, one of which is a solicitor’s strongroom, one of which is a convent, and one of which is a bank basement with four keyholders and no register of who they are.

story_seven_names/stage_varenne_house.alt: The Varenne House: A private hôtel in the eighth with a courtyard, eleven servants and a first-floor study that has a safe in it, a railway map on the wall and a daughter who is not where anybody thinks she is on any given evening.

story_seven_names/stage_veyrac_rooms.alt: The Rue de Grenelle: Not a house — a set of rooms where a rising man works eighteen hours a day with four secretaries and no wife.

story_seven_names/varenne.alt: Henri Varenne, Fifty-five, chairman of a bank, first name on the list, and the man who paid for the network that watched everybody including himself

story_seven_names/veyrac.alt: Étienne Veyrac, Forty-one, the dead minister’s closest friend, the man who gave the eulogy, and the man who arranged the killing

story_tidewall/ansett.alt: Commander Sabel Ansett, Commander of the eastern run

story_tidewall/bec.alt: Bec Tarrow, Longwatch archer, survivor of the eleventh gate

story_tidewall/cover.alt: Cover art for The Tidewall: Your sister died holding the wall.

story_tidewall/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for The Tidewall: Your sister died holding the wall.

story_tidewall/hollis.alt: Hollis Ferrant, Stillhand recruit, first on the roll

story_tidewall/odalys.alt: Drillmaster Odalys Verne, Drillmaster of the intake

story_tidewall/stage_beast_lines.alt: The Animal Lines: Pens, perches and a long roofed run where the orders keep everything they ride, fly, or answer to.

story_tidewall/stage_bright_hall.alt: The Bright Hall: A drum-shaped stone room sunk below the yard where the sorcerers of the wall bind their first element and argue about the second.

story_tidewall/stage_eleventh_gate.alt: The Eleventh Gate: A gatehouse and a low crossing where the ground comes up to meet the wall, which is why the tide chose it.

story_tidewall/stage_longwatch_post.alt: The Longwatch Post: A stone spur pushed out from the wall so archers can see along the face of it.

story_tidewall/stage_muster_yard.alt: The Muster Yard: Forty paces of frozen sand between the barracks and the wall stair, raked flat every morning by whoever came last to breakfast.

story_tidewall/stage_stillhand_tent.alt: The Stillhand Tents: Six canvas halls behind the yard, lit day and night, where the wall’s wounded are sorted by how long they have.

story_tidewall/stage_wall_walk.alt: The Wall Walk: The top of the Tidewall, wide enough for three abreast and nothing else, running east and west until it stops being a wall and starts being weather.

story_unbound/auber.alt: Reader Auber Kell, Concord reader, took the Oyan ruling

story_unbound/cover.alt: Cover art for The Unbound: Your school was dissolved. You were not.

story_unbound/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for The Unbound: Your school was dissolved. You were not.

story_unbound/renna.alt: Renna Vosk, Kiln instructor, holds your probation

story_unbound/sera.alt: Sera Ilm, Oyan student, sent to the Long Quiet

story_unbound/stage_concord_hall.alt: The Concord Hall: Where five schools that would rather not agree do it in writing anyway.

story_unbound/stage_confinement_house.alt: The Confinement House: Three rooms behind the Concord where people awaiting a ruling are kept comfortably and absolutely.

story_unbound/stage_contract_office.alt: The Contract Office: A long counter, five queues, and a board of work the schools have agreed to let students take.

story_unbound/stage_kiln_yard.alt: The Kiln Yard: A walled square of packed red earth behind the Kiln’s furnaces, warm even before sunrise.

story_unbound/stage_night_market.alt: The Night Market: Four streets of awnings along the water that only open after dark, selling food, salt, and the occasional thing a school would confiscate.

story_unbound/stage_oyan_house.alt: Oyan House: Your old school, doors sealed with a Concord band and a wax stamp, everything still inside it.

story_unbound/stage_river_stair.alt: The River Stair: Ninety wide stone steps from the upper city down to the water, where students from all five schools pass each other twice a day and pretend not to look.

story_unbound/tam.alt: Tam Ashgrove, Kiln full student, third year

story_understudy/cover.alt: Cover art for The Understudy: You know the part. You are second choice.

story_understudy/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for The Understudy: You know the part. You are second choice.

story_understudy/stage_directors_office.alt: The Director's Office: One chair for him and one for whoever is in trouble.

story_understudy/stage_green_room.alt: The Green Room: Two sofas that have outlived four principals, a kettle, and a noticeboard where the cast list goes up.

story_understudy/stage_rehearsal_room.alt: Rehearsal Room Two: Sprung floor, one wall of mirrors, and a piano nobody is allowed to move.

story_understudy/stage_stage.alt: The Main Stage: Nine hundred empty seats and a ghost light burning at centre.

story_understudy/stage_wardrobe.alt: Wardrobe: Rails to the ceiling and the smell of steam.

story_window_seven/ash.alt: Tobin Ash, Directorate internal security. He is not on this operation and he is on this street

story_window_seven/cover.alt: Cover art for Window Seven: Seven nights. One window. She waved.

story_window_seven/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Window Seven: Seven nights. One window. She waved.

story_window_seven/halden.alt: Director Elias Halden, Your handler. Twenty-nine years in the service and every one of them deniable

story_window_seven/juno.alt: Juno Vale, Orpheum Tower concierge, and the only person on this avenue who knows everybody’s business

story_window_seven/mara.alt: Mara Ellison, Your partner for seven nights. Four long-duration operations, no failures on paper

story_window_seven/selene.alt: Dr Selene Voss, The target. Cybernetics researcher, policy adviser, and the person who built the thing she is trying to destroy

story_window_seven/stage_apt_7c.alt: Apartment 7C: Blackout on every window but one, and a slit in that one the width of a lens.

story_window_seven/stage_directorate.alt: Directorate Nine: Two floors under a building that is legally a records agency.

story_window_seven/stage_orpheum_corrido.alt: The Seventh Floor: Carpet that eats sound, eleven doors, and a service riser at the far end with a lock that has been picked before.

story_window_seven/stage_orpheum_lobby.alt: Orpheum Lobby: Marble, a desk, and Juno Vale behind it at every hour anybody has ever checked.

story_window_seven/stage_orpheum_roof.alt: The Orpheum Roof: Plant machinery, a parapet, and a line of sight into the penthouse that the flat does not have.

story_window_seven/stage_riverside.alt: The Riverside: Old wharves converted into nothing in particular, a footbridge, and the third bollard from the east end with a cavity behind the plate.

story_window_seven/stage_the_avenue.alt: Kellis Avenue: Four lanes, a tram line down the middle, and eleven floors of glass on the far side.

story_window_seven/stage_the_subway.alt: Halberd Street Platform: Two lines, four exits, and a service every eleven minutes until one in the morning.

story_window_seven/stage_voss_penthouse.alt: The Penthouse: Eleven floors up and the whole of the avenue in one window.

story_window_seven/stage_voss_tower.alt: The Far Building: Newer than Orpheum and better staffed.

story_zero_throne/cover.alt: Cover art for Zero Throne: It knelt. Every camera saw it choose you.

story_zero_throne/cover.fr.alt: Cover art for Zero Throne: It knelt. Every camera saw it choose you.

story_zero_throne/eli.alt: Eli Vale, Nineteen, a student, and the grandson of the most hated man in the system, which is the only fact anybody has ever wanted from him

story_zero_throne/mina.alt: Mina Sorel, Lead mechanic in Hangar Four, twenty-three, raised in salvage yards, and the first person on this station to treat the machine as a machine

story_zero_throne/morrow.alt: Morrow, Vesper Zero’s onboard intelligence, awake in the dark for eighteen years, and the reason the machine chose anybody at all

story_zero_throne/orin.alt: Jace Orin, Helion commander, fifty-one, flew with Aren Vale, and has spent eighteen years being the reasonable man in rooms where that was not enough

story_zero_throne/rhea.alt: Rhea Kaine, Helion ace, twenty-four, decorated, and the only other person in the plaza who did not run when the machine came through the glass

story_zero_throne/stage_authority_office.alt: The Authority Offices: Eleven floors of neutral administration: customs, arbitration, the armistice secretariat, and an investigations division of nine people who have been quietly aware for years that their neutrality rests on something they have never been allowed to read.

story_zero_throne/stage_debris_belt.alt: The Belt: Eighteen years of a war’s worth of wreckage in a slow orbit, plus everything both sides quietly stopped declaring afterwards.

story_zero_throne/stage_freewake_berth.alt: The Far Berths: Three ships that belong to nobody, tied together by walkways somebody welded on without asking, with a galley in the middle that has been running continuously for nine years.

story_zero_throne/stage_ghost_archive.alt: The Ghost Archive: A floor of the Authority building that is not on the directory, holding the material both governments handed over in the forty-eight hours before the armistice on the understanding that nobody would ever look at it.

story_zero_throne/stage_lysandra_ruins.alt: Lysandra: Four million people lived here.

story_zero_throne/stage_main_hangar.alt: Hangar Four: A working bay: six berths, a gantry crane that squeals on the third pass, and Mina Sorel’s crew, who have been told a machine is coming and have not been told which one.

story_zero_throne/stage_memorial_plaza.alt: The Memorial Plaza: A hundred and forty metres of polished floor under a curved viewport with the planet turning in it, ringed by the names of the Lysandra dead in letters the height of a hand.

story_zero_throne/stage_meridian_concour.alt: The Concourse: The public spine of the station: shops, a transit ring, three competing news screens and forty thousand people who live here and have opinions about all of this.

story_zero_throne/stage_meridian_docks.alt: The Docks: Forty berths of freight, three of them permanently occupied by ships that have never filed a route.

story_zero_throne/stage_observation_loun.alt: The Observation Lounge: A quiet curved room high on the ring with the whole planet in the window and almost nobody in it, because everybody who works here stopped looking out of windows years ago.

story_zero_throne/stage_pilot_bar.alt: The Low Ring: Eleven tables under a bulkhead somebody has decorated with forty years of squadron patches from both sides, and one rule enforced by the woman behind the counter: nobody asks anybody what they did in the war.

story_zero_throne/stage_the_bunker.alt: The Command Level: Nine metres under a city that no longer exists, dry, dark and structurally perfect.

story_zero_throne/stage_vesper_hangar.alt: The Memorial Hangar: Sealed for eighteen years and no longer sealed.

story_zero_throne/talon.alt: Talon Reeve, Outer Compact ace, twenty-six, here officially as an observer and unofficially to make sure Helion does not walk off with the machine

story_zero_throne/venn.alt: Sera Venn, Helion intelligence director, thirty-eight, on this station to recover the machine without a public crisis, and the only person alive who has read the whole file

story_uncounted/stage_sablecourt.alt: Sablecourt: Forty thousand people on a grey-and-gold river, built around the largest Weighing House on the continent.

story_uncounted/stage_underbridge.alt: The Underbridge: Where the Unrated live, under and alongside the great bridge.

story_uncounted/stage_weighing_house.alt: The Weighing House: A domed hall of pale stone with a black assessing stone at its centre, worn concave by a century of hands.

story_uncounted/stage_southern_road.alt: The Southern Road: Aurelian’s wardenship, and the best-kept road on the continent: milestones, cut verges, a waystone every league with the current warden’s mark on it.

story_uncounted/stage_chalk_downs.alt: The Chalk Downs: The shallow edge of the Unkept, where the Assize gave up pricing and the grass gets long.

story_uncounted/stage_gilt_yard.alt: The Gilt Yard: Where the Warden of the Southern March keeps his horses when he is in the city, and where Grace sleeps, in a pen with a rail she could step over and has never once stepped over.

story_uncounted/stage_quill_row.alt: Quill Row: Notaries, scriveners, seal-cutters, and — four doors down, above a chandler’s — a very good woman named Bett who can make an Unrated into a Ninth for eleven silver and a favour.

story_uncounted/stage_halloway.alt: Halloway: A village of two hundred on the southern road with no warden since Perrin Alder’s uncle died in the spring.

story_uncounted/marrin.alt: Voss Marrin, Assessor of Sablecourt. Thirty-one years at the stone

story_uncounted/tsukasa.alt: Tsukasa, The Hollow. The only other person in the history of the Ledger to read dark on the stone

story_uncounted/grace.alt: Grace, A tiger three times the size of any tiger that has ever lived, and the best-loved animal in Orenne

story_uncounted/hale.alt: Cardew Hale, Assize officer, Reconciliations. The man they send when a page does not balance

story_uncounted/perrin.alt: Perrin Alder, Weighed Ninth, declared Hand, and told nobody why

story_uncounted/beck.alt: Beck Ardry, Weighed Ninth the same morning you did not weigh at all. Blade

story_uncounted/ithra.alt: Ithra Sen, Weighed Seventh, declared Staff, Assize-track and unbearable about it

story_uncounted/aurelian.alt: Aurelian, First Rank. Warden of the Southern March. The most loved person in Orenne

story_uncounted/rill.alt: Amaryllis Quist, Assize-licensed healer, on certification duty because nobody wants to be in a room with her
